00 — Origin

Built Between
Two Worlds

Raised between Bordentown, New Jersey and the culture of Dakar, Senegal. Two places, one foundation. Senegalese and Fulani heritage running through everything, American ambition driving what comes next.

Growing up between continents means growing up with two sets of values, two languages, two ways of reading a room. That duality is not a tension to resolve. It is a strategic advantage. The ability to move across cultures, communicate across contexts, and build across borders is what makes the work different.

Finance is the language that connects both worlds. Whether it is analyzing a deal structure in New Brunswick or understanding how capital flows through West African markets, the goal is the same: turn knowledge into leverage.

02 — Academic Work

Research & Papers

Original financial research applying institutional strategy frameworks to sport business contexts.

Case Study

Beyond the Wins: A Brand and Revenue Strategy for the Brooklyn Nets

BAASANA 2026 International Conference — Wagner College | The International Journal of Business & Applied Sciences (IJBAS)

This case study examines the Brooklyn Nets as a business enterprise, analyzing the structural financial and brand challenges preventing the franchise from building durable institutional value. Using publicly available financial data, franchise valuation reports, and comparative benchmarking against the Golden State Warriors, the study develops a five-pillar strategic framework addressing contracted revenue stability, arena utilization, community-rooted fan development, stakeholder conversion, and owned media strategy.

Executive Brief

Seydi Capital — Executive Brief, Issue 01

Beyond the Wins: Brand & Revenue Growth Strategy

A condensed strategic debrief on the Brooklyn Nets institutional challenge. The Nets gained cultural cachet since relocating to Brooklyn in 2012, but failed to convert visibility into durable trust. Revenue spikes with star arrivals and collapses with departures.

This brief outlines the five-pillar Seydi Framework: locking in contracted revenue, maximizing Barclays as a year-round platform, earning genuine community presence, converting fans into stakeholders, and building a Nets-owned media voice. Only 16.7% of YES Network viewers are from Brooklyn.
